items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...people like Sushan tell the story from the standpoint of a participant... And I, I think that, uh, your stories might very well corroborate the many things he tells.

ctx.x: Before I went to New York, yes. But I kept it up there. I, I, I bought music there. I used to go down to Segal Cooper's was a very big popular department store then. And I'd listen to the demonstrations there and buy music then. And, uh. Did you hear any ragtime players in New York? No. Any of you recall? No, no, not, none in particular. They, they played, of course, they demonstrated the music at the, at the stores, played it there. But, uh, somehow or other, uh, they didn't have those ragtime concerts, uh, or…

All right. That, that, that gives a pretty good background as, as to, uh, how you, uh, happened to notice the music that you were listening to. Now, uh, certainly, uh, people like Sushan tell the story from the standpoint of a participant. And apparently he was alert to, uh, the changes that were occurring from, uh, year to year in those early years. And I, I think that, uh, your stories might very well corroborate the many things he tells. Uh, you mentioned baby seals in vaudeville. Uh, there were an awful lot…

The minstrel show was a very popular thing at that time. And for a number of years after that, I don't know when it began to fade, maybe in the early twenties, I don't know, or the late, uh, 19s. But, uh, but, uh, at that time, minstrel shows were a big thing. And, uh, they, they, you've got some very good talent in minstrel shows. All good talent of all kinds. They didn't stand strictly on Negro stuff. But, uh, there were, there would be acrobatics and, uh, singers of other types there, you know, different acts,…
